# contextlake

> A local context layer for your AI tools: mirror your Git repositories, index them into a
> queryable knowledge graph + wiki, and serve it to AI editors over MCP. Offline-first, so
> agents answer from real source instead of guessing. Python CLI, published on PyPI.

## Get started

- [Overview](https://sayak.in/contextlake/docs): A local context layer for your AI tools: mirror your repos, index them into a knowledge graph, and serve it over MCP.
- [Quickstart](https://sayak.in/contextlake/quickstart): Install, bootstrap, and wire your editor, the whole Mirror -> Knowledge -> Serve path in a few minutes.
- [Configuration](https://sayak.in/contextlake/configuration): Config-file precedence and the full settings reference for the mirror layer.

## Build your knowledge base

- [Mirror repositories](https://sayak.in/contextlake/usage): Mirror your Git repos locally and keep them fresh: fetch, clone, update, most-active branch, verify, and audit, with branch-safety and scheduling.
- [Knowledge layer](https://sayak.in/contextlake/knowledge-layer): Turn the mirror into a queryable graph with search, a wiki, and connectors.
- [Index the code graph](https://sayak.in/contextlake/index-code-graph): Turn your mirrored repos into a queryable code graph: incremental indexing, and the full node and edge model across 14 languages, Terraform, SQL, and web topology.
- [Connect and enrich](https://sayak.in/contextlake/connect-enrich): Link repos to their issues, docs, and designs, manage sources, and pull grounded external facts into the knowledge layer with query-driven enrichment.
- [Semantic search](https://sayak.in/contextlake/semantic-search): Natural-language and hybrid graph-propagation retrieval: embed your code, tune the vector backend, and query across repos and languages.
- [Generate the wiki](https://sayak.in/contextlake/generate-wiki): Turn the graph into grounded, council-verified prose per repo: searchable, enrichment-aware, with a provenance footer.
- [Model providers](https://sayak.in/contextlake/model-providers): The pluggable embeddings and wiki backends: auto, built-in CPU, Ollama, OpenAI, Anthropic, and agent-CLI, with data-sharing posture and setup.
- [Bootstrap and keep fresh](https://sayak.in/contextlake/bootstrap): Run the whole pipeline in one command, compose the stages, and keep it fresh with cron or a git post-commit hook.

## Use it

- [Serve (MCP)](https://sayak.in/contextlake/serve): Expose the knowledge layer over MCP and wire your editors (Claude Code, Windsurf, Kiro) in one command.
- [Dashboard](https://sayak.in/contextlake/dashboard): A guided tour of the local, offline-first dashboard: the fleet overview, per-repo anatomy, the architecture graph, blast radius, and generating a wiki.
- [Visualize the graph](https://sayak.in/contextlake/visualize): Draw bounded, offline graph slices (`contextlake kb graph`) in HTML, DOT, Mermaid, or a class diagram, plus the composed namespace C4 diagram.
- [Ownership and SMEs](https://sayak.in/contextlake/ownership): Find who owns a repo or path and who to ask, ranked recency-weighted from git history (`contextlake kb owners` / `who_knows`), no config or index required.

## Understand it

- [Architecture](https://sayak.in/contextlake/internals): How all three layers work inside, the store, concurrency, branch selection, extraction, and the offline boundary.
- [Storage](https://sayak.in/contextlake/storage): Where contextlake keeps everything it generates, one store directory, never polluting your synced repos.
- [How contextlake compares](https://sayak.in/contextlake/comparison): What the continuously mirrored fleet gets you that other local, MCP-served code-graph tools don't have.
- [Benchmarks](https://sayak.in/contextlake/benchmarks): An honest, measured look at the token, cost, and correctness impact of connecting the contextlake MCP to your AI coding tools, new-code grounding first, plus search, maintenance, and the caveats.

- [Voice and tone](https://sayak.in/contextlake/style-guide-voice): Second person, present tense, warm and grounded: the voice defaults, word choice, and writing for every reader.
- [Page types and structure](https://sayak.in/contextlake/style-guide-structure): The concept, how-to, reference, and tutorial page types, each with a fixed skeleton, and how to structure a page.
